intro: まえに and あとで put one action on a timeline relative to another. The verb form in front of them is fixed, whatever the tense of the whole sentence: まえに always takes the dictionary form, because that action has not happened yet; あとで always takes the た-form, because that action is already finished.

skills.rule: Dictionary form + まえに = before; た-form + あとで = after; a noun takes の: 食事のまえに, 食事のあとで.
skills.explain:
まえに says the main action comes before X: 寝る前に歯を磨く. The verb before まえに is always in the dictionary form, even when the whole sentence is in the past: 日本に来る前に、少し日本語を勉強しました. Never 来た前に.

あとで says the main action comes after X: 食べた後で薬を飲む. The verb before あとで is always the た-form, even for the future: 仕事が終わった後で、飲みに行きませんか. Never 終わる後で.

Nouns take の: 食事の前に, 授業の後で. Event nouns work best (食事, 会議, 授業, 試合).

あと without で is also common, and it is the natural choice when a state or a stretch of time follows: 食べた後、しばらく休んだ. On its own, あとで also means "later": あとで電話します.
patterns: [noun] の まえに / あとで

examples.jp: 寝[ね]る{まえに}、歯[は]を磨[みが]きます。
examples.en: I brush my teeth before I go to bed.

examples.jp: 食事[しょくじ]の{あとで}、コーヒーを飲[の]みましょう。
examples.en: Let's have coffee after the meal.

examples.jp: 授業[じゅぎょう]の{まえに}、宿題[しゅくだい]を出[だ]してください。
examples.en: Please hand in your homework before class.

examples.jp: 日本[にほん]に来[く]る{まえに}、少[すこ]し日本語[にほんご]を勉強[べんきょう]しました。
examples.en: I studied a little Japanese before I came to Japan.

examples.jp: 仕事[しごと]が終[お]わった{あとで}、飲[の]みに行[い]きませんか。
examples.en: Shall we go for a drink after work?

examples.jp: 映画[えいが]を見[み]た{あとで}、みんなで感想[かんそう]を話[はな]しました。
examples.en: After the film, we all talked about what we thought of it.

contrast.note: てから stresses order or a precondition: 手を洗ってから食べて (wash first, then eat). It can also mean "since": 日本に来てから三年になる. あとで never means "since".
まで is "until": the main action continues up to that point. 寝るまで本を読んだ (read until I fell asleep) vs 寝る前に本を読んだ (read at some point before bed).
とき just marks when something happens, and the order depends on tense: 行くとき (on the way) vs 行ったとき (once there). まえに and あとで state the order outright.

mistakes.bad: 日本[にほん]に来[き]た{まえに}、日本語[にほんご]を勉強[べんきょう]しました。
mistakes.good: 日本[にほん]に来[く]る{まえに}、日本語[にほんご]を勉強[べんきょう]しました。
mistakes.note: まえに always takes the dictionary form, even in a past sentence.

mistakes.bad: 仕事[しごと]が終[お]わる{あとで}、電話[でんわ]します。
mistakes.good: 仕事[しごと]が終[お]わった{あとで}、電話[でんわ]します。
mistakes.note: あとで always takes the た-form, even about the future.

mistakes.bad: 食事[しょくじ]{まえに}手[て]を洗[あら]います。
mistakes.good: 食事[しょくじ]の{まえに}手[て]を洗[あら]います。
mistakes.note: A noun needs の before まえに and あとで.

skills.tip: Before = not yet = dictionary form. After = done = た-form.
